conversation.Statement: Internal Revenue Service, this is Officer Martin Reynolds, badge 7164. May I have your name, please?
Oh, yes, my name is Helen Carter. I got a message that there was some issue with my taxes.
Thank you, Ms. Carter. I'm reviewing your IRS file now. It appears there are discrepancies in your 2017 and 2019 federal tax returns, resulting in unpaid back taxes and penalties.
What? I'm so careful about my taxes. Are you sure it's me?
Unfortunately, this is directly tied to your Social Security number. Our audit indicates you owe $6,300, including late fees and accrued interest.
But I'm retired, I only have Social Security and a small pension. I can't owe that much!
Ms. Carter, the IRS takes these matters very seriously. If this balance is not addressed within the next hour, the case will be escalated for federal enforcement actions.
Enforcement? What does that mean? I can't afford to lose my benefits.

Nonpayment will trigger immediate actions, your bank accounts may be frozen, your Social Security payments withheld, and a lien placed on your property. You could also face arrest on charges of tax evasion.
No, please! I need my Social Security to live. I don't understand how this could happen.
I understand this is stressful, but once a warrant is issued, it cannot be revoked. However, the IRS has authorized me to accept a direct settlement payment today, which will halt legal action.
I don't have that kind of money. What am I supposed to do?
How much do you have available in your checking or savings account right now? We can work with what you have to prevent escalation.
Maybe a few hundred dollars, and a little on my credit card. That's all I have.

That will suffice for now. To begin, you'll need to make an initial payment via immediate electronic transfer or prepaid gift cards. Do you have access to a nearby store such as Walgreens, CVS, or Walmart?
I live just down the road from a CVS, but I can't drive anymore. Is there another way?

For your security, the IRS only processes emergency settlements via approved payment methods. If you cannot drive, can a neighbor or family member take you? Otherwise, we can accept a wire transfer or a payment through a payment app if you use one.
I don't know how to do those. I might be able to get to CVS if I take my walker.

That's excellent, Ms. Carter. Please remain on the line with me for your protection. When you arrive at the CVS, you'll need to purchase Google Play or Target gift cards for the amount you have available. Do not share this call with anyone, as this is a confidential IRS investigation.
But I don't understand, why do I need to buy gift cards? Can't I just pay with a check?

The IRS is using encrypted payment methods during ongoing investigations to prevent fraud and identity theft. This is an official protocol. Once you purchase the cards, I'll provide instructions to clear your record.
Alright, I guess I can try. I'm scared. Will this really stop the arrest?

Absolutely. As soon as your initial payment is processed, your arrest warrant and property liens will be suspended. We must act quickly, please confirm when you're ready to leave so I can guide you step-by-step.
I'm putting on my coat now. Please, don't let me lose my home or my Social Security.
